request: How large is the immigration court backlog and how has it changed over time?

reply.reply:
**EOIR had 3,558,995 pending immigration-court cases at the end of FY2024—up from over 1.5 million in FY2022’s first quarter; the backlog first exceeded 1 million in FY2019.**

- At the end of FY2024, EOIR had 3,558,995 pending immigration-court cases. (IN12492, PDF p. 4)
- In FY2024, immigration judges completed 701,749 cases—the agency’s largest annual total—but EOIR received an average of 148,663 new cases per month. (IN12492, PDF p. 4)
- The backlog first exceeded 1 million in FY2019, reached 1,405,386 cases by FY2021 year-end, and was above 1.5 million in FY2022’s first quarter. (R47077, PDF p. 21)
reply.reasoning: The latest located CRS data give a FY2024 year-end total and document that the backlog kept growing after crossing 1 million in FY2019. An earlier CRS report provides historical milestones through FY2022; these figures are from different reporting periods.
